label: EU(7)-PIM: prazosin, doxazosin, terazosin and urapidil
title: Prazosin, doxazosin, terazosin or urapidil in an older person
statement: Prazosin, doxazosin, urapidil and terazosin are named in the EU(7)-PIM list as potentially inappropriate medicines for older people. The reason given for each is a higher risk of low blood pressure on standing, dry mouth, and urinary incontinence or trouble passing urine. The list also names effects on the brain such as vertigo, light-headedness and sleepiness, and disease of the heart and blood vessels, including the blood vessels of the brain. The list advises a low starting dose and gradual changes when starting and stopping. As alternatives it suggests other blood pressure medicines, for example ACE inhibitors, chosen to suit the patient's other conditions. For terazosin, the suggested alternative blood pressure medicines apply when terazosin is used to treat blood pressure. The list includes terazosin regardless of why it is prescribed. The published entry also gives dose notes, which are not repeated here. This is the entrant's plain-words summary of the list entry, not the published wording.

The published wording is not reproduced, because the source marks part of it as taken from Micromedex and the right to reuse that part is not settled. The authors have not reviewed this adaptation.

plain_summary: Prazosin, doxazosin, terazosin and urapidil can cause a fall in blood pressure on standing, dizziness, sleepiness, a dry mouth and bladder problems in older people.

medicine_groups.name: Alpha blockers named in the list
medicine_groups.note: Count systemic urapidil, including Urapidil (Carinopharm) injection. Tamsulosin (for example Flomaxtra, and Duodart with dutasteride), alfuzosin (Xatral) and silodosin (Urorec) are alpha blockers for the prostate that this list entry does not name, and they do not count. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: For a Group A supply, suspect a finding at age 65 or older, report no finding below 65, and if age is missing report only a possible finding and ask for age confirmation. One supply of prazosin, doxazosin, urapidil or terazosin is enough, whatever the indication. A supply of urapidil injection counts.
cannot_be_seen: Why the alpha blocker was prescribed, for example blood pressure, prostate symptoms or nightmares after trauma. Also the patient's blood pressure lying and standing, whether the patient has had dizziness, fainting, falls or bladder problems, and supplies from a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether this alpha blocker is still the best choice at the patient's age, and whether the patient has had dizziness on standing, fainting, falls or bladder problems.
